releases.body: Desktop for Windows, macOS, and Linux, plus Android. Open the latest release and pick the file for your system.

server.body: Zips for Windows x64, Linux x64, and macOS Apple Silicon. On first run the wizard asks for the database, media, and port.

source.title: Source code

editor.q: Does Keres replace my text editor?
editor.a: It doesn't have to — but it can. Keres organizes the narrative universe, and each scene can also hold its prose: the manuscript view joins every scene into a single reading document, with export to Word, PDF, EPUB, HTML, Markdown, or plain text. Prefer drafting elsewhere? The prose stays optional; the planning still works.

browser.q: Does it run in the browser?
browser.a: Yes, at the Keres server itself (Docker or Keres Server), at /client. That client only connects to the API it was loaded from. Registering another server in the browser would be cross-origin again: web SQLite needs isolation on the same origin. On phone and desktop you can register any URL. Published stories live at /showcase.

offline.a: Not to plan. The client keeps everything on the device. A network is only needed to sync, collaborate, or publish on a server.

server.a: No. A story can live only on the device. A server comes in when you want the same universe on the phone and the PC, or when you want to collaborate.

languages.q: Which languages is the app in?
languages.a: Portuguese and English, in the client, the help, Keres Server, and this page.

collaborate.q: Can more than one person write it?
collaborate.a: With a server: invite friends, choose whether they read or edit, and comment on records. Without a server, you can hand off an import/export package.

cost.a: Keres is open software. You download the client and, if you want, run your own server. An operator of a public server may apply account limits — that is their decision, not the application's.

showcase.a: No. This is the project landing page. The showcase of published stories is a separate site, served by a Keres Server someone chose to run.
showcase.aLanding: Not this page. If this server's operator enabled publishing, its showcase is at /showcase, on this same server.
showcase.aLanding_official: Not this page. Published stories are in the showcase at /showcase, here on keres.me.

meta.title: Keres — Organize universes, connect narratives
meta.description: An offline-first story planning platform for phone, desktop, and the browser, served by the Keres server itself.
meta.description_official: An offline-first story planning platform for phone, desktop, and the browser, with the official Keres service at keres.me.

official.title: keres.me: the official server
official.lead: Run by the team behind Keres. Register there, or host your own server — the plans below are this server's offer.
official.lead_official: You are on keres.me, run by the team behind Keres. Register here, or host your own server — the plans below are the official ones.

offline.title: Offline-first for real
offline.body: Every story lives in a local SQLite database. Plan on a train, a plane, or the sofa. When a network and a server are there, sync ships the changes and handles version conflicts.

universe.title: The universe, and its manuscript
universe.body: Record who was in the scene, what changed hands, and which world rule that respects — and write the prose itself scene by scene, then read it as one document or export it.

anywhere.title: Phone, desktop, and browser
anywhere.body: The same client on Android, iOS, and the desktop app for Windows, macOS, and Linux. In the browser, the API serves the client at /client — only on that server's origin.

platforms.title: Where Keres runs
platforms.lead: One client, several ways to reach it. A server, when you want one.

mobile.title: Android & iOS
mobile.body: Native apps with local SQLite — APK and AAB on each release; plan on the phone, sync with the PC.

web.title: Browser
web.body: The API serves the client at /client, on the same origin. That page only talks to the server it was loaded from: pointing it at another API would be cross-origin, and SQLite in the browser would stop working.

desktop.title: Windows, macOS & Linux
desktop.body: Installer and portable executable, DMG, AppImage and Flatpak on every release.

server.title: Self-hosted server
server.body: A SQLite zip with a setup wizard, or Docker with Postgres — both serve the client, the showcase and the API.

product.title: One place for the whole story
product.lead: Open a story and the side menu lists every kind of element. Lists with search, filters, and favorites; records with relationships; graphs when space or choices ask for a map.

stack.title: How it is built
stack.lead: The same pieces described in the repository documentation.
stack.client: React Native + Expo, local SQLite, Zustand stores, and a custom sync engine.
stack.desktop: Electron wraps the client's web build for the desktop app. The same build, on the API, is the client at /client.
stack.api: Bun, Elysia, Drizzle. PostgreSQL in Docker; SQLite in the home Keres Server. Serves the web client at /client, on the same origin.
stack.admin: A React panel served by the API at /admin, for accounts, plans, and registration.
stack.shared: Entities, Zod contracts, and palettes shared across the apps.
